clue.text: Unassuming kid's first to leave desk during test

indicators.note: during places one piece within the span of the other, so it sits inside

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for UK vehicles

indicators.note: to leave says the named letter departs from the word desk

parts.note: taken as written before losing a letter

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word kid's

explanation.surface: A child's turn to get up from their desk in the middle of an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid's first' is K, which 'to leave' drops; 'during' puts the rest inside the MOT, the yearly British vehicle roadworthiness test.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone modest does not push themselves forward, which is exactly what unassuming describes.

clue.text: Word for 'doctor 'found in some dictionaries

indicators.note: found in means the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Lexicons list a particular term meaning physician.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside soME DICtionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: A medic is a medical practitioner or student, an informal word for a physician.

clue.text: Musician finally recognised stranger

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word recognised

parts.note: rummer means odder, from British rum meaning strange

explanation.surface: A performer is at last identified by a passer-by.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum is British slang for odd, so 'stranger' is RUMMER, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A drummer is a percussionist, a kind of musician.

clue.text: Dicky Rogers, team player of old

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for weak or faulty, so the letters are out of order

explanation.surface: Rogers, a poor team member from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' looks like a sportsman; here it is a record player.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereogram was a cabinet holding a radio and record deck, a home music centre of the 1960s.

clue.text: Gaelic language heard in refuge

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for refuge is spoken, and the entry matches its sound

parts.note: a refuge is a shelter

explanation.surface: Someone hears an old Celtic tongue spoken inside a safe house.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the word for refuge ends with the same sound as the entry. Shelta is a cant used by Irish Travellers, built partly on Irish Gaelic.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelta is the secret jargon of Irish Travellers, drawing heavily on Irish, so the clue calls it a Gaelic tongue.

clue.text: The way things go during court case is pitiful

indicators.note: during puts one piece within the span of the other

parts.note: a court case is heard at a hearing
a trend is the general direction things move in

explanation.surface: The run of events in a trial is pathetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heart-rending causes deep grief, so it is pitiful to see.

clue.text: See a female making bloomer, perhaps

parts.note: lo is an old word for see, look

explanation.surface: Look, a woman has made a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is a British crusty bread, not an error or a flower; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a type of crusty bread, an example of a loaf.

clue.text: Biting off edges of chocolate bar stuck on top of "99"

indicators.note: stuck on top of means placed above the next piece in this down entry
off means gone bad, so these letters are spoiled and rearranged
edges of takes the first and last letters of the word chocolate

parts.note: IC is 99 in a loose Roman reading, one less than a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone bites into a chocolate bar stuck in a 99 ice cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' shuffles the first and last letters of chocolate with bar into ACERB; 'stuck on top of' sets that above IC. A 99 is a British ice-cream cone with a chocolate flake, so the surface is a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerbic remarks are sharp and cutting, which is what biting means.

clue.text: Desire, but in an immoral way

parts.note: to desire is to want
but means only, as in but a child

explanation.surface: Craving, yet acting immorally.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting wantonly is behaving with reckless disregard for morals.

clue.text: Drinking pub beer regularly, father's getting plastered

indicators.note: drinking means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: dad is an informal word for father

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the words pub beer, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Dad has been knocking back ale at the local and is getting drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of pub beer and 'Drinking' puts them inside. 'plastered' looks like drunk, but here it means smeared, as with paint.
explanation.definitionFit: To daub is to smear thickly, as plaster or paint is spread over a surface.

clue.text: Write article about a miserable place in California

indicators.note: about means going around, so the first pieces surround the next ones

parts.note: to pen something is to write it
miserable means sad
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A writer pens a piece about a dismal Californian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the writing pieces round the misery, so the A and SAD split PEN after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasadena is a city near Los Angeles, home of the Rose Bowl.

clue.text: Animal carrying soldiers up to race meetings

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so the animal surrounds the rest

parts.note: an ass is a donkey

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
a nation is a people or race

explanation.surface: A beast of burden takes troops to the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the soldiers into SIG; 'carrying' puts that and the race inside the animal, just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An assignation is a secret meeting, often between lovers.

clue.text: Reimburse committee with some coppers -eight, you say?

indicators.note: you say tells us to speak the words that follow and enter what they sound like

parts.note: coppers are pennies, so some coppers are pence; said with eight it sounds like the end of the entry

explanation.surface: A committee repays someone with a handful of small change, eight pennies perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: COM is the dictionary abbreviation for committee. 'you say' covers both pence and eight: spoken together they make the sound PENSATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To compensate someone is to pay them back for a loss, which is what reimburse means.

clue.text: Help given to Elizabethans

indicators.note: given to suggests the letters belong to the word that follows and sit inside it

explanation.surface: Assistance is offered to people of the Tudor age.
explanation.walkthrough: The four letters sit inside ElizABETHans.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to aid or encourage someone, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Hetero? Gay? Male could get confused: this might help with decision making

definitions.text: this might help with decision making

indicators.note: could get confused signals that the letters are muddled up

explanation.surface: Someone straight or gay might be uncertain about how they make choices.
explanation.definitionFit: Game theory is the mathematical study of strategy, used to model choices among rivals.

clue.text: Bird mistaken for green pelican

indicators.note: mistaken signals that the letters of the phrase are wrongly arranged and must be sorted

explanation.surface: Someone has confused a large waterbird for a green pelican.
explanation.definitionFit: The peregrine falcon is a fast bird of prey, the quickest diver of all.

clue.text: Fruit fly, perhaps, better fed than the rest?

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
a fly is an example of a pest

explanation.surface: An insect on fruit eats more than the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumpest is the superlative of plump, so the fattest, best fed of all.

clue.text: Song released by me, old-fashioned with catchy end

parts.note: released means set free, unchained

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or worked, so the letters of old are reshaped
end picks out the last letter of the word catchy

explanation.surface: A singer brings out a dated tune with a memorable finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashioned' turns old into LOD; 'end' picks the last letter of catchy. 'old-fashioned' looks like one word, but it splits into fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Unchained Melody is a 1955 ballad, a hit for the Righteous Brothers and among the most recorded tunes ever.

clue.text: In important competition, be inclined to win everything

indicators.note: in places the leaning piece within the trophy

parts.note: a cup is a major contest, such as the FA Cup
to lean is to be inclined

explanation.surface: In a big tournament, someone tends to sweep the board.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean up is to win all the prizes or money on offer.

clue.text: Work no end over a 40-day period to get rich

indicators.note: no end says the last letter of the work is dropped

parts.note: an opus is a work, especially a musical one
Lent is the Christian season of forty days before Easter

explanation.surface: Working nonstop through Lent to become wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means lavishly wealthy, a showy kind of riches.

clue.text: Nobleman always chasing power

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is forever hungry for influence.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a member of the British nobility, such as a duke or baron.

clue.text: Rock parliament? His disappearance did

parts.note: a rock is a stone
a house is a chamber of parliament, such as the House of Commons

explanation.surface: A politician's vanishing shook the legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: John Stonehouse was a British Labour minister who faked his own drowning in 1974 and was later found in Australia, causing a scandal in Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue describes the minister whose faked death in 1974 rocked Westminster.

clue.text: Information about English verse form

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: dope is slang for inside information

explanation.surface: Facts concerning English poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: An epode is a lyric poem form with alternating long and short lines, as written by Horace.

clue.text: Prevent post being tampered with?

indicators.note: being tampered with says the letters of post have been interfered with

explanation.surface: Stop letters being interfered with.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop something happening is to prevent it.

clue.text: Authorise penalty

definitions.meaning: to authorise is to give official approval
a penalty is a punishment imposed, such as a trade embargo

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both official approval and a punitive measure, two nearly opposite senses.

clue.text: Very rainy round part of South Africa

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
rainy weather is wet
a round thing is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A region of South Africa is said to be extremely rainy.
explanation.walkthrough: Soweto is a township district of Johannesburg.
explanation.definitionFit: Soweto is a large urban area of Johannesburg, famous for the 1976 uprising.

clue.text: In time gone by, devout supporter of Catholicism

indicators.note: in places the devout piece within the period of time

parts.note: time gone by is the past
pi is informal British slang for pious, devout

explanation.surface: In days of old, a devout person backed the Roman church.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is short for pious, a common crossword word.
explanation.definitionFit: Papist is a hostile old label for a Roman Catholic, one loyal to the Pope.

clue.text: Entering wood, go about finding shrub

indicators.note: about here turns the whole assembled run backwards
entering means going in, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: elm is a kind of wood
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Searching the woods, someone wanders round and comes across a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entering' puts the attempt inside the tree, giving ELTRYM; 'about' then turns the whole run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is an evergreen bush with fragrant white flowers.
